en: to straighten; to hold something erect

examples.en: Try sitting with your back straight.
The lion holds its tail straight up.
You need to hold your body upright for your posture to improve.
We set the flagpole upright and drove it into the ground.
He puffed out his chest and held his upper body upright.

examples.ko: 고개를 곧추세우면 목이 아플 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes my neck hurts when I hold my head upright.

explain: 허리, 몸, 고개, 기둥처럼 길쭉한 것을 위로 곧게 세울 때 써요. '곤두세우다'는 귀, 신경, 털을 세울 때 주로 쓰니까 구별해서 써요. 스스로 서는 말은 '곧추서다'예요.

phrases.en: Hold your head up and look ahead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고개를 꼿꼿하게 든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to hold your head up stiffly and straight.

phrases.en: He was startled and straightened his body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누워 있거나 구부린 몸을 곧게 세울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when straightening a lying or bent body.

phrases.en: If you sit with your back held straight, your posture gets better.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어'로 이어서 앉는 모습을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with '-아/어' to describe how someone sits.

explain_en: It is used for making something long, such as your back, body, head or a pillar, stand straight up. '곤두세우다' is mainly for ears, nerves and fur, so keep them apart. The version where it stands by itself is '곧추서다'.

examples.en: My arm where the mosquito bit me is itchy.
I was itching to tell the story.

examples.ko: 새 게임이 하고 싶어서 손이 근질근질해서 참을 수 없어요.
examples.en: My hands are itching to play the new game and I can't wait.

examples.ko: 근질근질 가려워서 밤새 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: It itched so much that I couldn't sleep all night.
My back is itchy, could you scratch it for me?

examples.ko: 친구가 몸이 근질근질하다고 해서 같이 달렸어요.
examples.en: My friend said he was itching to move, so we ran together.

explain: 실제 가려운 느낌뿐 아니라 무엇을 하고 싶어서 가만히 있기 어려운 마음에도 써요. 보통 '근질근질하다' 형태로 말하고, '입이/손이/몸이 근질근질하다'처럼 몸의 일부와 같이 써요. '간질간질'은 살짝 건드리는 느낌이라 달라요.

phrases.example: 비밀을 들었는데 말을 못 해서 입이 근질근질해요.
phrases.en: I heard a secret but can't tell anyone, so I'm itching to say it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하고 싶은 마음을 참기 어려울 때 써요. 주로 비밀이나 재미있는 소식을 알고 있을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you can hardly hold back the urge to speak, usually when you know a secret or exciting news.

phrases.example: 하루 종일 앉아 있었더니 몸이 근질근질해요.
phrases.en: I've been sitting all day, so I'm itching to move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직이거나 운동하고 싶어서 가만히 있기 힘든 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes restlessness from wanting to move or exercise.

explain_en: Besides a literal itch, it is used for an urge to do something that makes it hard to sit still. It is usually said as '근질근질하다' and pairs with body parts, as in '입이/손이/몸이 근질근질하다'. '간질간질' is a light tickling feeling, so it is different.

en: to be sonorous; to be silvery

examples.ko: 시를 읊는 낭랑한 목소리가 교실에 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: A clear, ringing voice reciting a poem spread through the classroom.
The announcer's voice is clear and ringing, so it's nice to listen to.
The child read the book in a clear, ringing voice.
Even though she's old, my grandmother's voice is still clear and ringing.
It's not a ringing voice, but it's a warm one.
I still remember my teacher's clear, ringing voice.

explain: 주로 사람의 목소리나 낭독하는 소리가 맑고 또렷하게 울릴 때만 써요. 일상에서는 '목소리가 맑다'나 '또랑또랑하다'가 더 흔하고, '낭랑하다'는 글이나 방송에서 자주 보여요. 사물이나 풍경에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: I read the book in a clear, ringing voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낭랑하다'가 가장 자주 꾸미는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun 낭랑하다 most often modifies.

phrases.en: The student read the poem in a clear voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 내어 읽는 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how someone reads aloud.
phrases.en_equiv: to read in a clear voice

phrases.en: The teacher's voice is clear and ringing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 사람의 목소리를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in polite speech to describe a person's voice.

explain_en: It is used almost only when a person's voice or a reading aloud sounds clear and distinct. In daily talk '목소리가 맑다' or '또랑또랑하다' is more common, while '낭랑하다' often appears in writing and broadcasts. You don't use it for objects or scenery.

examples.ko: 대뇌는 생각하고 기억하는 일과 관련이 깊어요.
examples.en: The cerebrum is closely related to thinking and remembering.

examples.ko: 대뇌의 오른쪽과 왼쪽은 하는 일이 조금 달라요.
examples.en: The right and left sides of the cerebrum do slightly different jobs.

examples.ko: 사고로 대뇌를 다치면 말하기가 어려워질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you injure the cerebrum in an accident, speaking can become difficult.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 대뇌 그림을 그려 봤어요.
examples.en: We drew a picture of the cerebrum in science class.
The signals to move the body come from the cerebrum.

examples.ko: 대뇌와 소뇌가 함께 몸의 움직임을 조절해요.
examples.en: The cerebrum and cerebellum work together to control body movement.

explain: '뇌' 전체가 아니라 그중 가장 큰 윗부분을 가리켜요. 짝말은 '소뇌'이고, 일상에서는 그냥 '뇌'라고 해요. 과학이나 건강 수업에서 주로 나와요.

phrases.en: The cerebrum and the cerebellum do different jobs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝말인 '소뇌'와 함께 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said with its counterpart '소뇌'.

phrases.example: 대뇌 피질은 뇌의 가장 바깥 부분이에요.
phrases.en: The cerebral cortex is the outermost part of the brain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 수업에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A term that often appears in science classes.

phrases.en: Humans have a more developed cerebrum than other animals.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-가 발달하다'와 함께 써서 크기와 기능이 발전했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-가 발달하다' to say it has developed well.

explain_en: It refers not to the whole brain but to its largest upper part. Its counterpart is '소뇌' (cerebellum), and in daily life people just say '뇌'. It mainly appears in science and health lessons.

en: to move up and down; to raise and lower

examples.ko: 신나는 음악이 나오자 어깨가 저절로 들썩거려요.
examples.en: When lively music plays, my shoulders bounce on their own.
The floor shook from the thumping next door.
The child waited, fidgeting on the chair.
On World Cup days, the whole country is abuzz.
Please sit still and don't keep fidgeting.
The pot lid is rattling as the noodles boil.

explain: 몸이나 물건이 가볍게 위아래로 움직일 때 써요. 어깨, 엉덩이, 냄비 뚜껑뿐 아니라 '온 나라가 들썩거리다'처럼 분위기가 들뜬 모습에도 써요. '들썩이다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 음악에 맞춰 어깨를 들썩이며 춤을 췄어요.
phrases.en: I danced, moving my shoulders up and down to the music.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들썩거리다'와 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 짧아서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '들썩거리다', and a bit shorter, so it's widely used.

phrases.en: The child is so excited that he bounces up and down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동작이 계속 반복되는 모습을 부사로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adverb showing the movement repeating again and again.

phrases.example: 축제 때문에 온 동네가 들썩거리는 분위기예요.
phrases.en: The whole town is buzzing with excitement because of the festival.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 움직임뿐 아니라 마음이 들뜬 분위기를 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not only for body movement but also for an excited atmosphere.

explain_en: It is used when a body part or an object moves lightly up and down, like shoulders, hips or a pot lid. It also describes an excited atmosphere, as in '온 나라가 들썩거리다'. '들썩이다' is a common way to say the same thing.

examples.ko: 검사 결과 망막은 아무 이상이 없대요.
examples.en: The test results say there is nothing wrong with my retina.
My eyes felt blurry, so I had a retina exam.

examples.ko: 당뇨가 있으면 망막 상태를 정기적으로 살펴야 해요.
examples.en: If you have diabetes, you should check the condition of your retina regularly.

examples.ko: 밝은 빛이 망막을 상하게 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Very bright light can damage the retina.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 망막이 조금 얇다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said my retina is a little thin.

examples.ko: 눈앞이 번쩍거려서 망막에 문제가 생긴 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: Flashes appeared before my eyes, and I thought something was wrong with my retina.

explain: 안과에서 많이 듣는 말이에요. 눈 앞쪽의 투명한 막인 '각막'과 헷갈리지 않게 주의하세요. 한자가 다른 '망막하다(아득하다)'와는 관계없는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 눈을 크게 다치면 망막이 손상될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you badly injure your eye, the retina can be damaged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈 사고나 병 때문에 망막이 다쳤다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an eye injury or disease has damaged the retina.

phrases.example: 의사 선생님이 망막에 이상이 있다고 했어요.
phrases.en: The doctor said there is something wrong with my retina.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 검사 결과를 전하는 말로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to report test results from a doctor.
phrases.en_equiv: something is wrong with the retina

phrases.example: 당뇨가 있으면 망막 질환을 조심해야 해요.
phrases.en: If you have diabetes, you should watch out for retinal disease.
phrases.nuance_ko: '망막'에 병을 뜻하는 말을 붙인 짝말이고, 건강 정보에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing with 'disease' that often appears in health information.

explain_en: You hear this a lot at the eye doctor. Be careful not to confuse it with '각막' (cornea), the clear layer at the front of the eye. It is unrelated to '망막하다' (vast), which is written with different Chinese characters.

examples.ko: 할머니는 감기에 걸리면 민간요법으로 배숙을 만들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: When I had a cold, Grandma made me pear tea as a home remedy.

examples.ko: 민간요법만 믿고 병원에 안 가면 위험해요.
examples.en: It's dangerous to trust only folk remedies and not go to the hospital.

examples.ko: 꿀물은 목이 아플 때 쓰는 대표적인 민간요법이에요.
examples.en: Honey water is a typical home remedy for a sore throat.

examples.ko: 이 민간요법이 정말 효과가 있는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder if this folk remedy really works.
There are too many strange home remedies on the internet.

examples.ko: 시골에서는 아직도 민간요법을 쓰는 분들이 계세요.
examples.en: In the countryside, some people still use folk remedies.

explain: 병원 치료가 아니라 예전부터 전해 오는 방법으로 몸을 돌보는 것을 말해요. 한의원에서 하는 한방 치료와는 달라요. 몸이 심하게 아플 때는 민간요법보다 의사와 먼저 상의하는 게 안전해요.

phrases.example: 목이 아플 때 민간요법을 써 봤어요.
phrases.en: I tried a folk remedy when my throat hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원 약 대신 전해 오는 방법을 시도한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means trying a traditional remedy instead of medicine from a hospital.

phrases.en: Don't rely only on folk remedies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 심한데 병원에 안 가는 걸 걱정하며 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with concern when someone avoids the hospital despite illness.

phrases.en: If it hurts a lot, get treated at a hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 민간요법과 반대로 의사에게 받는 치료예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of a folk remedy: treatment from a doctor.

explain_en: It means caring for your body with methods passed down over time instead of hospital treatment. It is different from the herbal treatment given at Korean medicine clinics. When you are seriously ill, it is safer to consult a doctor first.

examples.en: My younger brother got up slowly and rubbed his eyes.

examples.ko: 자고 일어난 머리가 부스스해서 모자를 썼어요.
examples.en: My hair was messy after sleeping, so I put on a hat.
I don't want to go to school with messy hair.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 머리카락이 더 부스스해져요.
examples.en: On rainy days my hair gets even frizzier.
Grandfather slowly pulled himself up and spoke.
My perm has loosened and my hair is frizzy.

explain: 자다 일어나 느릿느릿 움직이는 모습, 그리고 머리카락이 엉키고 정리가 안 된 모습에 써요. 머리 이야기를 할 때는 '부스스하다' 모양으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I went to school with messy hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정리가 안 된 머리카락을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe untidy hair.

phrases.en: I sleepily opened my eyes in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자다 일어나 느릿하게 움직이는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for slowly moving after waking up.

phrases.en: My hair looks frizzy when it rains.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-해 보이다'는 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: -해 보이다 means it looks that way.

explain_en: It describes someone getting up slowly after sleeping, and also hair that is tangled and unkempt. When talking about hair, people mostly use the form '부스스하다'.

examples.en: The body secretes a sleep hormone at night.
The salivary gland is where saliva is secreted.

examples.ko: 식물이 이상한 냄새를 분비해서 벌레를 쫓아요.
examples.en: The plant secretes a strange smell to keep bugs away.
My body released adrenaline when I got nervous.

examples.ko: 이 세포는 독소를 분비할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This cell can secrete toxins.

examples.ko: 위가 위산을 너무 많이 분비하면 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts when the stomach secretes too much acid.

explain: 몸이나 식물이 어떤 물질을 안에서 밖으로 내보낼 때 써요. 과학 수업이나 건강 정보에서 나오는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않아요. '땀을 흘리다', '침이 나오다'처럼 쉬운 표현을 더 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 잠을 자는 동안 성장 호르몬이 분비돼요.
phrases.en: Growth hormone is secreted while you sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물질이 몸에서 나온다는 뜻으로, 과학 설명에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a substance is released by the body, common in science explanations.

phrases.en: It's hot, so I sweat a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '땀을 분비하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday way to say 'secrete sweat'.

phrases.example: 맛있는 음식을 보면 입에 침이 고여요.
phrases.en: When I see tasty food, my mouth waters.
phrases.nuance_ko: '침을 분비하다'를 일상에서는 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is how people say 'secrete saliva' in daily life.

explain_en: Used when a body or plant releases a substance from inside. It belongs to science class and health info, and is almost never used in casual talk, where phrases like 땀을 흘리다 or 침이 나오다 are more common.

examples.ko: 긴 산고 끝에 예쁜 딸이 태어났어요.
examples.en: After a long labor, a pretty daughter was born.

examples.ko: 아내가 열두 시간 동안 힘든 산고를 치렀어요.
examples.en: My wife went through a hard labor for twelve hours.
The labor pain was severe, so my mother had a very hard time.

examples.ko: 새 법안은 많은 산고 속에 만들어졌어요.
examples.en: The new bill was created through a lot of painful effort.

examples.ko: 산고의 고통은 겪어 봐야 안다고들 해요.
examples.en: They say you only know the pain of labor once you've been through it.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 십 년의 산고를 거쳐 완성됐어요.
examples.en: This novel was completed after ten years of painful labor.

explain: 아이를 낳을 때의 고통이라는 뜻 외에, 새로운 것을 만들어 내는 힘든 과정에도 비유로 써요. '산고 끝에', '산고를 겪다'가 대표적이에요. 출산 때 느끼는 아픔은 일상에서 '진통'이라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 오랜 산고 끝에 새 앱이 나왔어요.
phrases.en: After a long, painful process, the new app came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 과정 뒤에 결과가 나올 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when a result comes after a hard process.

phrases.example: 그 팀은 새 제품을 만들며 산고를 겪었어요.
phrases.en: The team went through great pains making the new product.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로운 것을 만들 때 겪는 어려움을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the hardship of creating something new.

phrases.example: 그녀는 첫째를 낳을 때 큰 산고를 치렀어요.
phrases.en: She went through great labor when she had her first child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 출산의 고통에도, 힘든 일에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for real childbirth pain and for hard undertakings.

explain_en: Besides the pain of giving birth, it is used figuratively for the hard process of creating something new. '산고 끝에' and '산고를 겪다' are typical. In daily speech, labor pains are also called '진통'.

examples.en: The children's mouths dropped open at the magician's hand movements.
The chef's hands move really fast.

examples.ko: 그 할머니는 바느질할 때 손놀림이 부드러워요.
examples.en: That grandmother's hands move smoothly when she sews.

examples.ko: 손놀림을 보니 오래 해 본 사람 같아요.
examples.en: Judging by the way his hands move, he seems experienced.
It's my first time, so my hands are still clumsy.
Please show me the hand movements slowly.

explain: 손을 움직이는 모습을 보고 솜씨를 말할 때 써요. '빠르다, 서툴다, 부드럽다'와 잘 어울리고, 타고난 재주를 뜻하는 '손재주'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: The clerk's hands move really fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 모습이 능숙할 때 칭찬으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a compliment when someone works skillfully.

phrases.en: It's my first time, so my hand movements are clumsy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 익숙하지 않아서 손이 서툰 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes clumsy hands from lack of experience.

phrases.en: She makes the dough with smooth hand movements.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 들어가지 않은 매끄러운 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes smooth, relaxed movements.

explain_en: Use it when judging skill from how someone's hands move, with words like '빠르다', '서툴다' and '부드럽다'. It is different from '손재주', which means natural manual talent.

examples.en: The nervous system sends signals throughout the whole body.
We learned about the nervous system in science class.

examples.ko: 이 병은 신경계에 문제가 생겨서 걸려요.
examples.en: This disease comes from a problem in the nervous system.

examples.ko: 잠을 못 자면 신경계가 약해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you can't sleep, your nervous system can weaken.

examples.ko: 신경계 그림을 보고 이름을 써 보세요.
examples.en: Look at the nervous system diagram and write the names.
The central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord.

explain: '계'가 붙은 '소화계', '순환계'처럼 몸의 한 체계를 가리켜요. '중추 신경계', '말초 신경계'처럼 나눠 말하는 경우가 많고, 수업이나 건강 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The brain and spinal cord belong to the central nervous system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신경계를 나누어 설명할 때 가장 먼저 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the first term used when dividing up the nervous system.

phrases.example: 할아버지는 신경계 질환 때문에 병원에 다니세요.
phrases.en: My grandfather goes to the hospital because of a nervous system disease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 건강 이야기에서 신경계에 생긴 병을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in medical talk for illnesses of the nervous system.

phrases.en: Children's nervous systems develop quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성장이나 발달을 설명할 때 '신경계'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 신경계 when explaining growth and development.

explain_en: Like '소화계' (digestive system) and '순환계' (circulatory system), the '계' ending names a body system. It is often divided into '중추 신경계' and '말초 신경계', and shows up in classes and health talk.

examples.ko: 돼지 염통을 볶아서 먹어 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever tried stir-fried pig heart?

examples.ko: 닭 염통은 쫄깃해서 꼬치로 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: Chicken hearts are chewy and taste good on skewers.
My grandmother calls the heart by the old word 'yeomtong'.
We made a stir-fry with beef heart.
Please give me one geun of heart at the butcher shop.

examples.ko: 옛날 소설에는 염통이라는 말이 가끔 나와요.
examples.en: The word 'yeomtong' sometimes appears in old novels.

explain: '심장'의 우리말이지만 지금은 몸 이야기에서는 '심장'을 써요. 염통은 돼지, 닭, 소의 내장 부위를 말하는 음식 이야기나 어르신들의 말에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: One chicken heart skewer, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 주문하거나 이야기할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when ordering or talking about food.

phrases.en: The heart meat gets chewier the more you chew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식으로 먹는 염통의 식감을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the texture of heart meat as food.

phrases.en: I got so surprised that my heart is racing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸 이야기에서는 '염통' 대신 '심장'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: When talking about the body, use 심장 instead of 염통.

explain_en: It is the native Korean word for 심장 (heart), but in talk about the body people now use '심장'. 염통 is mostly heard when talking about the heart of a pig, chicken or cow as food, or in the speech of older people.

en: to be chubby; to be plump

examples.en: The baby's cheeks are so plump and adorable.
He gripped the toy tightly with his chubby hand.
The puppy has put on weight and become plump.
I ate dumplings with plump shrimp inside.
My younger sibling had a chubby face as a child.
Being called chubby sounds like praise for being cute.

explain: '통통하다'와 비슷하지만 작고 귀엽게 살이 올라 있는 느낌이 더 강해요. 아기의 볼, 작은 손, 강아지처럼 귀여운 대상에 잘 어울려요. 몸집이 큰 어른에게는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: The puppy's plump cheeks are cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀엽게 살이 오른 얼굴이나 몸 부분에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits cute, plump parts of the face or body.

phrases.en: The baby has become chubby in just one month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해졌어요'를 붙여 살이 올라 귀여워진 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '해졌어요', it describes the change to cute chubbiness.

phrases.en: A plump cat is lying down.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오동통하다'보다 더 널리 쓰는 말이고, 귀여운 느낌은 조금 덜해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more general word than '오동통하다', with a bit less of the cute feel.

explain_en: It is similar to '통통하다' but has a stronger feel of being small and cutely plump. It suits cute things like a baby's cheeks, small hands or puppies, and is not usually used for large adults.

examples.en: The nurse injected medicine into my arm.

examples.ko: 타이어에 공기를 주입하는 데 오 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes five minutes to pump air into the tire.
The teacher didn't force knowledge into us.
The government decided to inject money into the market.

examples.ko: 기계에 물을 주입한 다음에 켜 주세요.
examples.en: Please turn it on after pouring water into the machine.

examples.ko: 아이들에게 한 가지 생각만 주입하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't drill just one idea into children.

explain: 주입하다는 어떤 것을 속에 밀어 넣거나 흘려 넣을 때 써요. 약이나 연료 같은 물질에도 쓰고, 생각이나 지식을 억지로 가르칠 때 '주입하다'라고도 해요. 그래서 '주입식 교육'은 외우게만 하는 교육을 가리켜요.

phrases.example: 주입식 교육 때문에 생각하는 힘이 약해졌다는 말이 있어요.
phrases.en: rote-style education
phrases.nuance_ko: 이해보다 외우기 중심으로 지식을 넣어 주는 교육 방식을 말해요. 보통 좋지 않은 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A teaching style that stuffs in knowledge by memorization rather than understanding. Usually said negatively.

explain_en: 주입하다 means pushing or pouring something into something else. It works for substances like medicine and fuel, and also for forcing ideas or knowledge into someone. That is why '주입식 교육' refers to rote-style education.

examples.ko: 홍채는 눈동자 둘레에서 색이 있는 부분이에요.
examples.en: The iris is the colored part around the pupil.

examples.ko: 이 스마트폰은 홍채 인식으로 잠금이 풀려요.
examples.en: This smartphone unlocks with iris recognition.
Everyone's iris pattern is different.

examples.ko: 제 눈은 홍채 색이 짙은 갈색이에요.
examples.en: My eyes have a dark brown iris color.
I had an iris examination at the hospital.

examples.ko: 밝은 곳에서는 홍채가 동공을 작게 만들어요.
examples.en: In bright places, the iris makes the pupil smaller.

explain: 일상에서는 '눈동자'라고 하지만 병원이나 보안 기술에서는 '홍채'라고 정확히 말해요. '홍채 인식'은 지문 인식처럼 본인 확인에 쓰는 기술이에요.

phrases.en: That child's eyes are brown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '홍채'보다 '눈동자'를 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, 눈동자 is used far more often than 홍채.

phrases.en: At the airport, they confirm identity with iris recognition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈의 홍채 모양으로 본인을 확인하는 기술을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to technology that verifies a person by the pattern of their iris.

phrases.en: Iris color is a little different for each person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈 색깔을 조금 더 정확하고 과학적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more precise, scientific way of talking about eye color.

explain_en: In daily life people say '눈동자', but in hospitals and security technology the precise word '홍채' is used. '홍채 인식' (iris recognition) is an identity-check technology like fingerprint recognition.

en: to become pop-eyed; to become round-eyed

examples.en: I was so startled that my eyes went wide.

examples.ko: 선물 상자를 열자 아이 눈이 휘둥그레져요.
examples.en: When the gift box opens, the child's eyes go wide.

examples.ko: 눈이 휘둥그레진 손님들이 가격표를 다시 봤어요.
examples.en: The customers, wide-eyed, looked at the price tag again.

examples.ko: 친구가 눈이 휘둥그레져서 무슨 일이냐고 물었어요.
examples.en: My friend's eyes went wide and he asked what was going on.
There were more than a few things that made my eyes go wide.

examples.ko: 처음 보는 큰 건물에 눈이 휘둥그레질 거예요.
examples.en: Your eyes will go wide at the huge building you're seeing for the first time.

explain: 놀라거나 신기해서 눈이 동그랗게 커질 때 써요. 주어는 보통 '눈'이고, '눈이 휘둥그레지다'를 한 덩어리로 기억하면 편해요. 놀람 외에 감탄이나 부러움에도 쓰고, '눈이 휘둥그레져서 쳐다보다'처럼 뒤 동작과 이어 말해요.

phrases.example: 아이가 커다란 케이크를 보고 눈이 휘둥그레져서 쳐다봤어요.
phrases.en: The child stared wide-eyed at the huge cake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀란 눈과 뒤의 행동을 한 문장으로 이어 말할 때 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Handy for linking the surprised eyes with the action that follows.

phrases.en: I watched the magic show with wide eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '눈'을 꾸며 주는 관형형이에요. 놀라거나 신기한 표정을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for 눈, used to picture a surprised or amazed look.

phrases.en: My eyes went round when I saw the price.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 '휘둥그레지다'가 놀람이 더 크게 느껴져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but 휘둥그레지다 feels more intensely surprised.

explain_en: Use it when your eyes widen from surprise or wonder. The subject is usually '눈', so it is easiest to learn '눈이 휘둥그레지다' as one chunk. It covers admiration and envy as well as shock, and often links to a following action, like '눈이 휘둥그레져서 쳐다보다'.
